findings.summary: crates/athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: The own-stem rule refuses ordinary criteria when an item's only own stem is a weak verb.
findings.evidence: In the corpus request at refusal_corpus.rs:1711-1714, part 3 is 'Cover the flag with a test'. 'flag' is dropped because part 1 also has it, 'test' is on the stop list, and 'with' is dropped too (or, worse, counts; see the stop-list finding). That leaves {cover}, and the plan says so itself ('keeps `cover`, needs one shared stem'). A natural criterion for part 3, such as 'A unit test checks the --json flag output' or '`cargo test` runs a case for `athena status --json`', does not contain 'cover', so the part counts as uncovered and the reading is refused. This affects every request whose parts share their nouns (the usual case for a feature, its docs and its test). Every Steward request has bullets and must pass this rule (steward.rs:619-624). That makes it likely the newly refused share exceeds the 10% hold limit the plan itself cites. No corpus case has a paraphrased criterion that covers a part using only shared nouns. Fix: Give the reader a sure, deterministic way to show coverage. A criterion that names the item's marker ('(3)', 'part 3', 'item 3') covers that item whatever its stems. The refusal message tells the reader to cite the marker, the way `Term X:` and `Consumers:` lines repair other checks. Keep stem overlap as the fallback for unnumbered bullets. Add an Accept corpus case with a paraphrased criterion that cites '(3)', and a Refuse twin without the citation, so the cost of the heuristic is visible.
findings.location: Approach: COVERAGE USES ONLY AN ITEM'S OWN STEMS; Decision 2

findings.summary: Shape A grants a split to any modal 'land/do/ship ... in/as the change' sentence, and with no marker named it exempts every item.
findings.evidence: Shape A is: move verb (including land, ship, do, handle, deliver), then up to 4 object words, then in/into/as/to/for, an optional determiner, an optional adjective, and a noun from {job, change, PR, pull request, request}. Under that rule, 'The tests may land in the change.', 'You can do it as a change to the parser.' and 'It may ship in one PR.' all match. 'one PR' is the opposite of a split. These words are everywhere in Athena requests ('the change', 'the request'). The plan says a clause that names no marker exempts every item. So one such sentence turns the gate off for the whole request. None of the plan's negative cases covers this shape. Fix: Require a split signal inside the destination: an adjective from {separate, follow-up, later, next, another, own}, or a plural noun with a count adjective (several, multiple). Treat the determiners this, the, one and same as blocking. Add 'The tests may land in the change.', 'It may ship in one PR.' and 'You can do it as a change to the parser.' as negative rows in the permission table and as Refuse corpus cases.
findings.location: Approach: SPLIT EXEMPTION, Shape A; Decision 4

findings.summary: Any out_of_scope item that names a marker counts as a deferral, so out_of_scope items that only narrow a part are refused.
findings.evidence: The plan says: 'out_of_scope: an item naming a marker counts without a phrase and without the past guard (a covered item listed as out of scope is a contradiction).' Naming a marker does not put the item out of scope. Readers routinely narrow a covered part in out_of_scope, e.g. 'For (2), the web view is not changed' or 'Part 3 beyond the CLI test'. Under this rule each of those refuses a reading that covers every part. No corpus case pins a narrowing out_of_scope item. Fix: In out_of_scope, count a marker only when the item is the whole part. Either require a deferral phrase as in the other fields, or require that the item is the bare marker or restates the part's own stems and nothing more. Add an Accept corpus case where out_of_scope narrows a covered part ('(2): the web view is unchanged').

findings.summary: The stop list names only domain words, so common English words of 4 or more letters ('with', 'that', 'from', 'each', 'when', 'into', 'only') count as distinctive stems.
findings.evidence: The stop list is given as 'test, tests, pass, passes, change, changes, described, existing, job, part, request, fmt and similar'. In part 3 'Cover the flag with a test', 'with' would be an own stem. Part 3 would then need only 1 shared stem (min(2, ceil(2/2))), so any criterion containing 'with' covers it. That defeats the silent-omission case `parts-dot-third-silently-omitted` that the plan relies on. Fix: State that the stop list includes English function words of 4 or more letters, list them in the code comment, and pin 'with', 'that' and 'from' as not distinctive in the stem unit test.
findings.location: Approach: DISTINCTIVE STEM; plan step 4 stop list

findings.summary: The plan does not say whether backticked or quoted spans are removed from criteria before stems are taken. If they are, the Steward accept case fails.
findings.evidence: request_parts removes quoted and backticked spans from the request (without_quoted_spans, terms.rs:86). Real readers write criteria like '`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes'. The only own stem of 'fmt, clippy and test pass' is 'clipp'. If criteria went through the same span removal, that bullet would never be covered, and a real Steward reading would be refused. Fix: State that criteria, summary and other reading text are tokenised whole, with quoted spans kept. Add a Steward Accept case whose clippy criterion is in backticks.

findings.summary: The fixture it describes cannot be built: StewardRequest refuses a body that holds a dash line.
findings.evidence: StewardRequest::from_change turns every dash or star line into an acceptance bullet (steward.rs:607-617). StewardRequest::new returns Err('the body has lines that start like acceptance bullets') when request_text_acceptance finds bullets beyond the acceptance list (steward.rs:586-589). So a render whose body holds a non-acceptance dash line cannot exist. Fix: Build this unit test from a hand-written request, with a body dash line before an 'Acceptance:' label line. Keep from_change only for the standard-bullet cases.
findings.location: Demonstration for criterion 2 (StewardRequest render with a non-acceptance dash line)

findings.summary: The dependents list omits the proposal-apply request generator and its bullet-request test, and the code-health generated request.
findings.evidence: reading.rs:8445-8447, PROPOSAL_REQUEST, copies the shape that proposals.rs accept_request writes, including the bullet '- Add the default with id = "x".'. reading.rs:8476 asserts refuser_for(...) == None for that request. code_health.rs:1362 asserts its generated request carries 'Acceptance:\n- '. Neither appears in the dependents list. The proposals test happens to pass only if 'default' and 'defaults' reduce to the same stem. Fix: Add proposals.rs accept_request (test reading.rs scope_limit_proposal_apply_shape) and the code_health request generator to the dependents list. Name the stem behavior the proposals test depends on.
findings.location: Dependents: request text shapes the new check reads

findings.summary: The reason the plan gives for stripping markers is doubtful, and copying request text into fake criteria can trip other checks whatever the marker.
findings.evidence: check_scope_limit reads a limit from the criterion's words through change_limit (checks.rs:709-713), not from a list marker. So a copied bullet such as 'Only src/a.rs may change' is refused with or without its '- '. The fake reader's capability defaults to the first schema enum, so the reading is a change reading and check_scope_limit applies. Fix: State the real reason for stripping markers (the producer and verifier fakes split criteria on '. '). Note that copied bullets which limit files can still be refused by check_scope_limit; the end-to-end fake test should include one such request, or the fake should skip limiting lines.
findings.location: Approach: FIXTURES THAT THIS CHANGE BREAKS (fake.rs)

summary: The plan matches the accepted reading. It answers most of the round-1 findings with concrete rules, places the new step last in refusing_check (checks.rs:532-546), keeps is_bullet and request_text_acceptance unchanged, and fixes the fixed-reading fakes at their seams. I read the plan's anchors in checks.rs, steward.rs:560-636, fake.rs:223-403, terms.rs:55-208 and refusal_corpus.rs:1676-1748, and grepped every caller of refusing_check, check_reading_acceptance and check_reading_text. They mostly hold. Three rules have obvious false positives, so the verdict is revise. First, the own-stem coverage rule leaves an item with only one weak verb stem. The plan's own example, part 3 'Cover the flag with a test', keeps only 'cover', so an ordinary criterion for it ('a unit test checks the --json flag output') is refused. Second, the split exemption's Shape A accepts plain singular destinations such as 'in the change' or 'as a change'. A sentence like 'Tests may land in the change.' would switch the gate off for every item. Third, the out_of_scope rule refuses any out_of_scope item that names a marker, even when the item only narrows a part that is covered. Minor gaps: the stop list does not say it includes common English words such as 'with'; it is not stated whether backticked text is removed from criteria; one criterion-2 demonstration cannot be built, because StewardRequest::new refuses a body with dash lines; and the dependents list omits the proposal-apply request shape and its test.
